meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out he had a zero from his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. So on what basis did you enter it?
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. Turn the screen around.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.
I'm writing down those times. He writes in other places and pastes things in, Hale, that's not a crime. Whatever this turns into, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
In this file. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, and a pasted document doesn't tell you where it came from. What else do you have?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.
I'll want a copy of that outline. Students change their minds in two weeks, Hale. What exactly are you proposing?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

I'll check it tonight. If you're about to offer him a rewrite, it's done privately, not in front of his class, and I want "nothing goes on file" in writing. That's to put this behind him, not because he did anything.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Then answer the question, Hale. Is that what you're offering, or not?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay he had weeks for, that's not the same thing. I've seen enough documents, Hale. Yes or no on the rewrite.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

"Holds up." Okay, then the zero comes out of the gradebook today, the rewrite is private and done before December 1, and the new mark replaces it. I want all of that in an email by tomorrow morning, with my name and your principal's on it.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Okay. Which day, and who else will be in the room? Ten minutes, Hale.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

Comfortable isn't on the table. A date before the end of next week, just you and Owen in the room, and a fair test on the same outcomes, not a trap. And the zero is gone from that gradebook before he sits down.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Copy your principal, and write the words "nothing goes on his record" exactly like that. If it's not in my inbox by eight tomorrow morning, I'm in her office at nine.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
That the mark went in before anyone called me, against procedure 4.2, and that it won't happen to Owen again. That's all.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Okay. I'll be watching for it, Hale.
Thank you for coming in.
Don't thank me yet. Eight o'clock, Hale.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Not tomorrow. He gets the date in your email first, with at least two days' notice, and the zero is already gone when he walks in.
